instructions: Empty any remaining liquid from the bottle.
Lightly rinse if required by your local recycling program.
Crush the bottle to save space and replace the cap.
Check local recycling rules for accepted plastic resin numbers (PET #1, HDPE #2).
plastic_bottle.caution: A visual prediction cannot confirm the exact plastic resin. Black plastics and unmarked polymers may need special sorting.

instructions: Keep paper and cardboard clean and completely dry.
Flatten cardboard boxes to save bin capacity.
Remove plastic tape, bubble wrap, and plastic film.
Separate and discard grease-soaked or food-soiled sections.
paper_cardboard.caution: Greasy pizza boxes, wax-coated cartons, and heavily contaminated paper cannot be recycled with regular paper.

instructions: Rinse food and beverage glass containers.
Separate by color (clear, green, brown) if your municipal program requires it.
Remove metal or plastic caps and lids.
Handle broken glass carefully, wrapped in paper or cardboard for safety.
glass.caution: Drinking glasses, cookware (Pyrex), ceramics, mirrors, and window panes melt at different temperatures and cannot go into standard bottle banks.

instructions: Empty and rinse remaining food or beverage residue.
Aluminum cans and steel/tin cans are widely accepted in curbside recycling.
Keep lids attached or push them inside the can.
Do not crush aerosol cans.
metal_can.caution: Ensure aerosol cans are completely empty before recycling. Never recycle cans that contained paint, chemicals, or automotive fluids in standard bins.

instructions: Separate food scraps, fruit peels, vegetable cuttings, and coffee grounds from packaging.
Place in your household compost bin or municipal green waste bin.
Use certified 100% compostable bags if bags are required.
Follow local rules regarding meat, dairy, and cooked food composting.
organic_waste.caution: Not every municipal compost facility accepts bones, fats, or pet waste. Never include plastic stickers or plastic food packaging.

instructions: Take electronics, cables, batteries, and appliances to an authorized e-waste drop-off site.
Remove rechargeable batteries and tape battery terminals before drop-off.
Wipe personal data from phones, laptops, and storage devices.
Many electronic retailers offer free electronics take-back programs.
electronic_waste.caution: Never place lithium-ion batteries or electronics into household trash or standard recycling bins—they pose severe fire risks.

instructions: Clean and dry wearable clothing and shoes for local charity donation.
Torn or unwearable textiles can be dropped off at dedicated textile recycling bins.
Repurpose clean fabric scraps into household cleaning cloths.
Keep textiles out of curbside recycling bins as they jam sorting machinery.
textile.caution: Mildewed or chemically soiled fabrics must be disposed of in general waste to prevent contamination.

instructions: Keep substances in their original labeled containers.
Never mix chemicals, solvents, or household cleaners together.
Transport securely upright to a licensed Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) depot.
Check your municipal hazardous waste collection schedule.
hazardous.caution: Corrosive, flammable, toxic, or reactive chemicals must never be poured down the drain, onto the ground, or into trash bins.

instructions: Inspect the product label for specific disposal or recycling icons.
If the item is a composite material (mixed plastic and metal/paper), place it in residual landfill waste unless parts can be separated.
Check your municipal waste lookup tool for local sorting instructions.
Keep potentially hazardous materials separate from general refuse.
general_waste.caution: When in doubt, do not 'wishcycle' (tossing unknown items into recycling). Non-recyclables contaminate entire batches of clean recyclables.
